api/Cosmos.Kernel.Core.Scheduler.ISchedu.summary: Interface IScheduler Namespace Cosmos.Kernel.Core.Scheduler Assembly Cosmos.Kernel.Core.dll A scheduling policy: everything that decides which thread runs when. The mechanism around it (the thread registry, the lifecycle transitions, the timer-tick entry, the register save and restore) is fixed. Install an implementation with SetScheduler(IScheduler). Every hook runs in the kernel's most sensitive window. Most are called with interrupts already masked, and the two scheduling hooks run inside the timer interrupt itself; each member below says which. No hook may block, park, or wait, and none may allocate on the tick path. Four get no mask from the manager (SetPriority(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread, long), GetPriority(SchedulerThread) and the two run-queue diagnostics) and must take MaskInterrupts() themselves before touching the run structure. The spinlock around SetPriority(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread, long) is not a substitute: it excludes another caller, not the tick. Several hooks have no mechanism-side caller yet, because the kernel runs on one CPU and nothing in-tree sets priorities. Implement them, but do not expect them to be exercised. Two rules hold for every hook. Each must tolerate being called more than once for the same thread, and each must tolerate an empty SchedulerData slot, because OnThreadExit(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) clears it and a thread can lose its record between a tick and the hook that observes it; that is why a hook reads the slot with as and never a cast. A record written by a different policy is never handed to a hook: SetScheduler(IScheduler) re-homes every live thread through OnThreadExit(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) on the outgoing policy and OnThreadCreate(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) on the incoming one. Inspired by Ekiben's EkibenScheduler trait. [Experimental("COSMOS0001")] public interface IScheduler Properties Name Display name for this policy, used in boot logs and reported on the ring as SchedulerInfo.SchedulerName. string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods Balance(PerCpuState, PerCpuState[]) Rebalance load across CPUs, honouring Pinned. Dormant until SMP lands: nothing calls it today. void Balance(PerCpuState cpuState, PerCpuState[] allCpuStates) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU asking for work, or offering it. allCpuStates PerCpuState[] Every CPU the scheduler manages. GetPriority(SchedulerThread) Report a thread's current priority in the same policy-defined units SetPriority(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread, long) takes. Called from thread context with no guard at all, on every thread snapshot the SchedulerInfo facade takes, so it must not mutate anything and must mask itself if it reads something a tick can be rewriting. long GetPriority(SchedulerThread thread) Parameters thread SchedulerThread Thread to query. This hook receives no PerCpuState. Returns long The thread's priority, or 0 when the policy does not track one for it. GetRunQueueCount(PerCpuState) Report how many threads are waiting in the run structure. Read-only introspection for the SchedulerInfo facade, called from thread context with no guard, so guard it yourself with MaskInterrupts() if a concurrent tick could be mutating the structure underneath it. Masking inside the hook makes one call atomic and no more: a caller that counts and then reads each index needs its own mask around the whole walk, or the tick can rotate the queue between the calls. int GetRunQueueCount(PerCpuState cpuState) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU to inspect. Returns int The number of queued threads. GetRunQueueThread(PerCpuState, int) Report the queued thread at a position. Same calling context and same guarding duty as GetRunQueueCount(PerCpuState). SchedulerThread? GetRunQueueThread(PerCpuState cpuState, int index) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU to inspect. index int Queue position, from 0 to GetRunQueueCount(PerCpuState) exclusive. Returns SchedulerThread The queued thread, or null when the index is out of range. InitializeCpu(PerCpuState) Allocate this policy's per-CPU bookkeeping into SchedulerData on cpuState. Called once per CPU by SetScheduler(IScheduler), in thread context with interrupts masked across the whole swap, so no tick observes the window between the outgoing policy's ShutdownCpu(PerCpuState) and this call. void InitializeCpu(PerCpuState cpuState) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU whose state to attach bookkeeping to. OnPickFailed(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) Put back a thread the mechanism picked but could not switch to. Declared for completeness; nothing calls it today. void OnPickFailed(PerCpuState cpuState, SchedulerThread thread) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU the pick was made for. thread SchedulerThread Thread that could not be switched to. OnThreadBlocked(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) Remove the thread from the run structure and save whatever must survive the park. Called for a block and for a timed sleep, with interrupts masked. void OnThreadBlocked(PerCpuState cpuState, SchedulerThread thread) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU the thread was queued on. thread SchedulerThread Thread parking. OnThreadCreate(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) Allocate this policy's per-thread bookkeeping into SchedulerData on thread. Do not queue the thread yet: OnThreadReady(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) does that. Called with interrupts masked, once for a new thread and once for every live thread the policy inherits through SetScheduler(IScheduler). An inherited thread arrives in whatever state it is in: Ready ones are handed to OnThreadReady(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) right after, blocked and sleeping ones come back through it when they wake, and a Running one keeps running and must be accounted as runnable without being queued. The boot thread arrives that way at startup as well. void OnThreadCreate(PerCpuState cpuState, SchedulerThread thread) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU the thread is being created on. thread SchedulerThread Thread entering this policy's management. OnThreadExit(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) Remove the thread everywhere and drop its bookkeeping. Called with interrupts masked, before the mechanism unregisters the thread. void OnThreadExit(PerCpuState cpuState, SchedulerThread thread) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU the thread was managed on. thread SchedulerThread Thread terminating. OnThreadMigrate(SchedulerThread, PerCpuState, PerCpuState) Move a thread's bookkeeping, and any virtual-time base, between CPUs. The mechanism never calls this; a policy calls it from its own Balance(PerCpuState, PerCpuState[]). void OnThreadMigrate(SchedulerThread thread, PerCpuState fromState, PerCpuState toState) Parameters thread SchedulerThread Thread being migrated. fromState PerCpuState CPU the thread is leaving. toState PerCpuState CPU the thread is joining. OnThreadReady(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) Make the thread runnable: place it and insert it into the run structure. Called for a first start, for a wake, and for a sleep expiry, so it arrives both from thread context with interrupts masked and from interrupt context, either the timer tick waking a sleeper or a device ISR signalling a waiter. It is the hook most likely to fire twice for one thread, so guard against inserting it twice. void OnThreadReady(PerCpuState cpuState, SchedulerThread thread) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU the thread is queued on. thread SchedulerThread Thread becoming runnable. OnThreadYield(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) Re-insert a thread that gave up the CPU while still runnable. Called from an explicit yield in thread context with interrupts masked, and from the preemption path in interrupt context, where it runs after PickNext(PerCpuState) has already chosen the replacement: the outgoing thread is not a candidate for the switch it is being preempted by. void OnThreadYield(PerCpuState cpuState, SchedulerThread thread) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU the thread is queued on. thread SchedulerThread Thread giving up the CPU. OnTick(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread, ulong) Account the elapsed time and decide whether to preempt. Called from the timer interrupt, on every tick, and it is the only hook that runs on a fixed schedule: keep it allocation-free. bool OnTick(PerCpuState cpuState, SchedulerThread current, ulong elapsedNs) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU being ticked. current SchedulerThread Thread running on it. elapsedNs ulong The timer's configured period in nanoseconds, not a measurement of how long the thread actually ran. Charging it to Thread.TotalRuntime is the policy's job, and the ring's busy-CPU-time reading depends on the policy doing it. Returns bool true to request a reschedule, which runs PickNext(PerCpuState) before this interrupt returns. PickNext(PerCpuState) Pick the next thread to run. Called in interrupt context, on every reschedule. The outgoing thread is not in the run structure at this point; it goes back through OnThreadYield(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) afterwards. SchedulerThread? PickNext(PerCpuState cpuState) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU to schedule. Returns SchedulerThread The thread to switch to, or null to fall back to the CPU's idle thread. Remove the thread you return from the run structure: the manager re-inserts the outgoing thread through OnThreadYield(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) after this call, and does not remove the incoming one, so leaving it queued grants it a second turn. The manager does not check the thread's state either, so never return one that is dead or parked. SelectCpu(SchedulerThread, uint, uint) Choose a starting CPU for a new or migrating thread, honouring Pinned. Dormant until SMP lands: nothing calls it today, and this hook receives no PerCpuState. uint SelectCpu(SchedulerThread thread, uint currentCpu, uint cpuCount) Parameters thread SchedulerThread Thread being placed. currentCpu uint CPU the thread is on now. cpuCount uint Number of CPUs the scheduler manages. Returns uint The CPU to place the thread on. SetPriority(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread, long) Change a thread's priority. The meaning is policy-defined: Stride reads it as a ticket count, a real-time policy would read it as a priority level. Reached only through SetPriority(uint, SchedulerThread, long), whose per-CPU spinlock excludes another caller but not the timer, so this hook must take MaskInterrupts() itself before touching the run structure. void SetPriority(PerCpuState cpuState, SchedulerThread thread, long priority) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU whose state guards the update. thread SchedulerThread Thread to reprioritize. priority long New policy-defined priority. ShutdownCpu(PerCpuState) Release the per-CPU bookkeeping, leaving a clean slot for the incoming policy. Called once per CPU by SetScheduler(IScheduler) before the replacement is initialized, in thread context with interrupts masked, like InitializeCpu(PerCpuState). Thread slots are not cleared here; see SchedulerData. void ShutdownCpu(PerCpuState cpuState) Parameters cpuState PerCpuState CPU whose state to release bookkeeping from.

api/Cosmos.Kernel.Core.Scheduler.Schedul.summary: Class SchedulerExtensible Namespace Cosmos.Kernel.Core.Scheduler Assembly Cosmos.Kernel.Core.dll Base class for objects that can hold scheduler-specific extension data. [Experimental("COSMOS0001")] public abstract class SchedulerExtensible Inheritance object SchedulerExtensible Derived PerCpuState SchedulerThread Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties SchedulerData Scheduler-specific data. Each scheduler defines its own class and stores an instance here from its IScheduler lifecycle hooks (InitializeCpu(PerCpuState), OnThreadCreate(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread)), and clears it again in ShutdownCpu(PerCpuState) and OnThreadExit(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread). One slot is the whole budget: a policy needing several values defines one class holding them. A policy swap moves every live thread with it: SetScheduler(IScheduler) hands each one to the outgoing policy's OnThreadExit(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) and then to the incoming policy's OnThreadCreate(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread), so a hook is never handed a record another policy wrote. Read it with as, never a cast, all the same: a hook can still meet an empty slot, because OnThreadExit(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) clears it and a thread can lose its record between a tick and the hook that observes it. A cast that fails does so inside the timer interrupt, and as costs nothing on a hook that handles null anyway. public object? SchedulerData { get; set; } Property Value object

[Experimental("COSMOS0001")] public static class SchedulerManager Inheritance object SchedulerManager Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Fields DefaultQuantumNs The interval the boot path asks the platform to arm the scheduler timer at, in nanoseconds (10 ms), and the slice the built-in Stride policy tunes itself against. It is a starting value, not a running fact: a driver can retune the timer afterwards, so read Cosmos.Kernel.Core.Scheduler.SchedulerManager.TickPeriodNs for what the kernel is actually ticking at. A policy is free to preempt on its own terms and need not treat either number as its slice. public const ulong DefaultQuantumNs = 10000000 Field Value ulong NanosecondsPerMillisecond Nanoseconds per millisecond, used to convert sleep timeouts to timestamp units. Public so other kernel components (e.g. timer drivers) can share the unit conversion. public const ulong NanosecondsPerMillisecond = 1000000 Field Value ulong Properties Current The installed scheduler, or null before SetScheduler(IScheduler) has run. public static IScheduler? Current { get; } Property Value IScheduler IsReady Whether the boot path has built the per-CPU state, which is what makes the rest of this class usable. Blocking primitives (and drivers built on them) must check this before touching GetCpuState(uint): with the scheduler feature compiled out, or before its library initializer runs, there is exactly one execution context, so callers fall back to spin/polled paths instead of blocking. public static bool IsReady { get; } Property Value bool Methods GetCpuState(uint) Returns the scheduling state of a CPU, or null when IsReady is false. public static PerCpuState? GetCpuState(uint cpuId) Parameters cpuId uint CPU to look up. The count is on the ring as SchedulerInfo.CpuCount; a policy normally takes the state it needs from its hook parameters instead. Returns PerCpuState Exceptions IndexOutOfRangeException cpuId is not a managed CPU and the scheduler is ready. Before it is ready this returns null for any value. GetPriority(SchedulerThread) Returns a thread's priority as reported by the installed scheduler (GetPriority(SchedulerThread)). public static long GetPriority(SchedulerThread thread) Parameters thread SchedulerThread Thread to query. Returns long MaskInterrupts() Masks maskable interrupts on the current CPU until the returned scope is disposed. Schedulers use this around the entry points the manager does not guard: SetPriority(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread, long), GetPriority(SchedulerThread), the two run-queue diagnostics hooks, and any tuning setters the policy exposes of its own. The spinlock SetPriority(uint, SchedulerThread, long) holds is not a substitute: it excludes another caller, and the tick path takes no lock at all. The tick hooks, the thread-lifecycle hooks and the two per-CPU lifecycle hooks are already called with interrupts masked. public static InterruptMaskScope MaskInterrupts() Returns InterruptMaskScope SetPriority(uint, SchedulerThread, long) Changes a thread's priority through the installed scheduler (SetPriority(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread, long)). Interpretation is scheduler-specific. public static void SetPriority(uint cpuId, SchedulerThread thread, long priority) Parameters cpuId uint CPU whose run structure the update rewrites. thread SchedulerThread Thread to reprioritize. priority long New priority value. SetScheduler(IScheduler) Installs a scheduling policy. Every live thread moves with it. The outgoing policy, if any, gets OnThreadExit(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) for each thread it was managing and then ShutdownCpu(PerCpuState) on every CPU. The incoming policy gets InitializeCpu(PerCpuState) on every CPU, then OnThreadCreate(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) for each live thread and OnThreadReady(PerCpuState, SchedulerThread) for those that were waiting in a run queue, so no thread is left behind in a run structure that no longer exists. The whole swap runs with interrupts masked, so no tick can land in the window where the incoming policy is installed but its per-CPU state does not exist yet, and every CPU reschedules on its next interrupt exit so the incoming policy picks from its own queue. public static void SetScheduler(IScheduler scheduler) Parameters scheduler IScheduler Scheduler to install.

api/Cosmos.Kernel.HAL.Interfaces.Devices.summary: Interface IBlockDevice Namespace Cosmos.Kernel.HAL.Interfaces.Devices Assembly Cosmos.Kernel.HAL.Interfaces.dll Interface for block storage devices (SATA, NVMe, virtio-blk, etc.). Block-level read/write only; partitioning and filesystems sit above this. Error contract: ReadBlock(ulong, ulong, Span<byte>), WriteBlock(ulong, ulong, ReadOnlySpan<byte>) and Flush() throw on failure (device error, timeout, out-of-range request). A return without an exception means the operation completed on the device. public interface IBlockDevice Properties BlockCount Total number of addressable blocks on the device. ulong BlockCount { get; } Property Value ulong BlockSize Block size in bytes (typically 512 or 4096). ulong BlockSize { get; } Property Value ulong Name Human-readable device name, unique per device instance (e.g. "sata0", "nvme0n1"). string Name { get; } Property Value string Methods Flush() Flush the device's volatile write cache so previously completed writes are durable. No-op on devices without a volatile cache. void Flush() ReadBlock(ulong, ulong, Span<byte>) Read whole blocks starting at blockNo into data. void ReadBlock(ulong blockNo, ulong blockCount, Span<byte> data) Parameters blockNo ulong Logical block address to start reading from. blockCount ulong Number of blocks to read. data Span<byte> Destination buffer; must be at least blockCount * BlockSize bytes. WriteBlock(ulong, ulong, ReadOnlySpan<byte>) Write whole blocks starting at blockNo from data. Completion means the device accepted the write; durability against power loss is only guaranteed after Flush() returns. void WriteBlock(ulong blockNo, ulong blockCount, ReadOnlySpan<byte> data) Parameters blockNo ulong Logical block address to start writing to. blockCount ulong Number of blocks to write. data ReadOnlySpan<byte> Source buffer; must be at least blockCount * BlockSize bytes.

Remarks Layout mirrors Unix mode bits: Permissions: owner/group/other read, write, execute (bits 0-8) Special: sticky, setgid, setuid (bits 9-11) File type: high nibble encodes the type (bits 12-15); mask with FileTypeMask. The file-type nibble is an enumerated field, not a bit set, even though the type carries FlagsAttribute for the permission bits. Its values overlap: BlockDevice is CharacterDevice | Directory, SymbolicLink is CharacterDevice | RegularFile, and Socket is Directory | RegularFile. api/Cosmos.Kernel.System.Diagnostics.Thr.summary: Enum ThreadKillResult Namespace Cosmos.Kernel.System.Diagnostics Assembly Cosmos.Kernel.System.dll Outcome of RequestKill(uint). public enum ThreadKillResult : byte Fields Killed = 1 The thread was removed from its run queue and terminated, on the managed side too: a Join() on it returns, and it reads as stopped, exactly as after a return from its entry point. MarkedForExit = 2 The thread was running and has been marked dead. The next reschedule stops putting it back in a run queue, so it never runs again, but nothing reaps it: the registry slot, the stack, the allocation context and the policy's bookkeeping are released only by a thread's own exit path, which a thread stopped this way never reaches. Prefer letting a thread return from its entry point. NotFound = 0 No live thread has the requested ID. Also the answer when no scheduler is installed and when scheduler support is compiled out, since neither leaves a registry to search. RefusedBlocked = 4 The thread is registered but is neither running nor queued: blocked, sleeping, created and never started, or already marked for exit by an earlier request. Blocked and sleeping threads sit outside the run queues with their share already returned to the policy, so terminating one from here would return it twice; wake it first. RefusedIdle = 3 The request named an idle thread, which cannot be killed.

This is the supported way for kernels to emit debug output that a host can capture; on QEMU the stream appears on the -serial device. Writes are synchronous, allocation-free for strings and numbers, and usable from the earliest phase of BeforeRun onward. MemoryInfo Diagnostic view of the kernel's physical-memory and garbage-collector statistics, plus a forced collection. Every figure is a property, and each is a plain field read with no allocation, so they are safe to poll from a monitor loop at display refresh rate. The two collector counters are read independently rather than as a pair, so a collection landing between two reads shows up in one of them and not the other. Managed-heap figures beyond these counters come from the BCL (GetGCMemoryInfo()). All reads are allocation-free and safe to poll from a monitor loop; snapshots of threads that are being rescheduled concurrently may be one tick stale. Three shapes report "nothing there", and which one a member uses follows from what it is. A plain read answers with its own empty value, so CpuCount, ThreadCount, ThreadSlotCount, TickPeriodNs, BusyCpuTimeNs and GetRunQueueCount(uint) are 0 and SchedulerName is null before the scheduler exists, with no separate error channel. A read that must hand back a whole snapshot cannot express absence in the snapshot itself, so it is a Try and the bool carries that answer. The snapshot is taken without locking the scheduler, so fields of a thread that is being rescheduled concurrently may be one tick stale. This is a projection of SchedulerThread, the thread control block on the experimental scheduler seam, and it is narrower on purpose. It carries what a monitor can render off an unlocked read: identity, state, and two totals. The checksum differs by version, and this is the only place the two differ: a zero checksum means "not computed" over IPv4 and is illegal over IPv6, so the build constructors that receive the payload write a real checksum, and the ones that leave the payload for the caller leave the field zero for WriteChecksum() to fill in. Exceptions ArgumentException The two addresses belong to different IP versions. UdpPacket(Address, Address, ushort, ushort, ushort) Creates a UDP datagram with an uninitialized payload area of dataLength bytes, of the version both addresses belong to. Every header and length field is written during construction and never recomputed, so the payload must be filled in before the packet is sent. The checksum field is left zero: call WriteChecksum() once the payload is in place, which is mandatory over IPv6 and optional over IPv4. public UdpPacket(Address source, Address dest, ushort srcPort, ushort destPort, ushort dataLength) Parameters source Address The source address. dest Address The destination address. srcPort ushort The source port. destPort ushort The destination port. dataLength ushort The payload length in bytes. Exceptions ArgumentException The two addresses belong to different IP versions. UdpPacket(Address, Address, ushort, ushort, ushort, MACAddress) Creates a UDP datagram with an uninitialized payload area of dataLength bytes and a preset destination MAC address, which skips neighbor resolution. Every header and length field is written during construction and never recomputed, so the payload must be filled in before the packet is sent. The checksum field is left zero: call WriteChecksum() once the payload is in place, which is mandatory over IPv6 and optional over IPv4. public UdpPacket(Address source, Address dest, ushort srcPort, ushort destPort, ushort dataLength, MACAddress destMac) Parameters source Address The source address. dest Address The destination address. srcPort ushort The source port. destPort ushort The destination port. dataLength ushort The payload length in bytes. destMac MACAddress The destination MAC address to write into the Ethernet header. Exceptions ArgumentException The two addresses belong to different IP versions. UdpPacket(byte[]) Parses a UDP datagram from a raw Ethernet frame, picking the internet version from the EtherType. The instance aliases rawData without copying, so later changes to the array are visible through this packet. Header properties are parsed once during construction. public UdpPacket(byte[] rawData) Parameters rawData byte[] The raw frame bytes, starting at the Ethernet header. Exceptions ArgumentException The frame carries neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 header. Properties Checksum Gets the checksum field as parsed from the header, a snapshot taken at construction. Reads zero on a datagram whose payload the caller still has to fill in and checksum. public ushort Checksum { get; } Property Value ushort DestinationIP The destination address of the carrying internet packet. public Address DestinationIP { get; } Property Value Address DestinationPort Gets the destination port, a snapshot parsed from the UDP header at construction. public ushort DestinationPort { get; } Property Value ushort Network The internet packet carrying this datagram: the frame buffer, the addresses, and the version-specific half of the checksum. Pass it to Send(InternetPacket) to transmit the datagram. public InternetPacket Network { get; } Property Value InternetPacket RawData The complete wire image of the frame, Ethernet header included. public byte[] RawData { get; } Property Value byte[] SourceIP The source address of the carrying internet packet. public Address SourceIP { get; } Property Value Address SourcePort Gets the source port, a snapshot parsed from the UDP header at construction. public ushort SourcePort { get; } Property Value ushort UdpDataLength Gets the payload length in bytes: UdpLength minus the 8-byte UDP header. public ushort UdpDataLength { get; } Property Value ushort UdpLength Gets the value of the UDP length field: the 8-byte UDP header plus the payload. It is a snapshot parsed from the header at construction and is never recomputed. public ushort UdpLength { get; } Property Value ushort Methods GetUdpData() Returns a fresh copy of the UDP payload (the bytes after the 8-byte UDP header). Each call allocates; the packet's underlying buffer is not exposed, so mutating the returned array does not affect the packet. public byte[] GetUdpData() Returns byte[] A new array holding the payload bytes. ToString() Returns a string with the source and destination endpoints and the payload length. public override string ToString() Returns string A human-readable summary of the packet. VerifyChecksum() Checks the stored checksum against the datagram and the pseudo-header, as a receiver does. Sums the whole datagram on every call. public bool VerifyChecksum() Returns bool True when the datagram is intact. A stored zero counts as intact over IPv4, where it means the sender computed no checksum, and as corrupt over IPv6, where every datagram must carry one. WriteChecksum() Computes the checksum over the datagram as it stands and stores it, then re-parses the header snapshots. Call this once the payload is complete, which is mandatory over IPv6, where a zero checksum is illegal, and optional over IPv4, where it means "not computed". A computed value of zero is stored as all ones, as RFC 768 requires, so that it is never mistaken for an absent checksum. public void WriteChecksum()

api/Cosmos.Kernel.System.Network.html.summary: Namespace Cosmos.Kernel.System.Network Namespaces Cosmos.Kernel.System.Network.ARP Cosmos.Kernel.System.Network.Config Cosmos.Kernel.System.Network.DNS Cosmos.Kernel.System.Network.IPv4 Cosmos.Kernel.System.Network.IPv6 Cosmos.Kernel.System.Network.TCP Cosmos.Kernel.System.Network.UDP Classes Address Represents an IP address: an Address4 or an Address6. EndPoint An address and port pair, of either IP version. EthernetPacket An Ethernet frame, the root of the packet hierarchy. The frame lives in RawData; every header property is a snapshot parsed from that buffer at construction time and is not refreshed by later writes to the buffer. Derived types lay their headers into the same buffer from their constructors, including checksums: there is no separate finalize-before-send step. InternetPacket The internet layer of a frame: an IPv4 or an IPv6 packet. A transport protocol composes one of these instead of deriving from it, which is what lets a single transport class serve both versions: the internet packet owns the frame buffer, reports where the transport section starts and how long it is, computes the transport checksum with its own pseudo-header, and queues itself on the outgoing buffer that resolves its kind of neighbor address. NetworkManager Manages network devices. NetworkStack Manages the Cosmos networking stack. Structs MaskedAddress The result of masking an address: its bytes, most significant first, indexable by octet. A stack-only value, so it is never boxed or stored. NetworkAdapter A handle to one of the network devices HAL enumeration registered. Obtained from GetAdapter(int) or Primary, and handed back to the ring to inspect that device or to configure it with Enable(NetworkAdapter, Address, Address, Address). Enums AddressFamily The IP version an Address belongs to. AddressNumericStyle The number base an IPv4 address is parsed from or formatted in.

An extended partition contains a singly-linked list of EBR sectors; each EBR holds one logical partition entry plus an optional pointer to the next EBR. Convention used: Logical-entry start LBA is relative to the EBR sector that holds it. Next-EBR pointer is relative to the extended partition's start LBA (the standard convention). The first EBR always sits at the extended partition's start LBA. Each subsequent EBR is placed immediately after the prior logical's data. public static class Ebr Inheritance object Ebr Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Methods MoveLogical(IBlockDevice, ulong, int, ulong) Rewrite the start of the logicalIndex-th logical partition so its data begins at the absolute host LBA newStartSector. Caller is responsible for making sure data at the new range is what's expected (use MoveWithData(IBlockDevice, PartitionLocation, ulong) for a data-copying move). public static bool MoveLogical(IBlockDevice device, ulong extendedStartSector, int logicalIndex, ulong newStartSector) Parameters device IBlockDevice extendedStartSector ulong logicalIndex int newStartSector ulong Returns bool Parse(IBlockDevice, ulong) Walk the EBR chain rooted at extendedStartSector and return one entry per logical partition. api/Cosmos.Kernel.System.Storage.html.title: Namespace Cosmos.Kernel.System.Storage | Cosmos Gen 3
api/Cosmos.Kernel.System.Storage.html.summary: Namespace Cosmos.Kernel.System.Storage Classes Ebr EBR (Extended Boot Record) chain parser and editor. An extended partition contains a singly-linked list of EBR sectors; each EBR holds one logical partition entry plus an optional pointer to the next EBR. Convention used: Logical-entry start LBA is relative to the EBR sector that holds it. Next-EBR pointer is relative to the extended partition's start LBA (the standard convention). The first EBR always sits at the extended partition's start LBA. Each subsequent EBR is placed immediately after the prior logical's data. Gpt GPT (GUID Partition Table) parser / writer. Reads / writes the primary header at LBA 1 plus the partition entry array starting at LBA 2. 512-byte sectors assumed (matches every block device this kernel currently exposes). GptPartitionEntry Single parsed partition. Sector positions are absolute on the host disk. Mbr MBR (Master Boot Record) partition table parser / writer. Operates on any IBlockDevice with 512-byte sectors. MbrPartitionEntry Single MBR partition entry. Sector positions are absolute on the host disk. Partition Block-device view of a single partition on a host disk. Read/Write are translated to the host LBA space by adding StartSector. PartitionManager High-level partition lifecycle (create / delete / resize / move) on top of Mbr and Gpt. Auto-detects the table type per call. MoveWithData(IBlockDevice, PartitionLocation, ulong) physically copies sectors before rewriting the table; the other operations are pure table edits. StorageManager Manages block storage devices. Structs PartitionManager.PartitionLocation Identifies a partition by its absolute LBA range on the host disk.

api/Cosmos.Kernel.System.Timer.AlarmMana.summary: Class AlarmManager Namespace Cosmos.Kernel.System.Timer Assembly Cosmos.Kernel.System.dll Runs callbacks after a delay on a dedicated kernel thread. Alarm callbacks run in thread context, so they may block, allocate and use scheduler primitives, unlike the interrupt-context callbacks of Schedule(Action, TimeSpan). Requires the scheduler; resolution is bounded by the scheduler tick. The scheduling calls themselves also run in thread context only. Every member here takes the alarm list's mutex and parks if it is held, so calling one from an interrupt handler, a TimerManager callback included, parks inside the handler and hangs. The TimerManager members mask interrupts instead of parking and have no such restriction. public static class AlarmManager Inheritance object AlarmManager Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Methods Cancel(ulong) Cancels a pending alarm. public static bool Cancel(ulong id) Parameters id ulong ID returned by Schedule(Action, TimeSpan) or ScheduleRecurring(Action, TimeSpan). Returns bool True when the alarm was pending and has been cancelled; false when it had already fired or the ID is unknown. Schedule(Action, TimeSpan) Schedules a callback to run once after the specified delay, in thread context. public static ulong Schedule(Action callback, TimeSpan delay) Parameters callback Action Method to invoke when the delay expires. delay TimeSpan Delay before the alarm fires. Returns ulong The alarm ID to pass to Cancel(ulong), or 0 when the alarm could not be scheduled because the scheduler is not running. ScheduleRecurring(Action, TimeSpan) Schedules a callback to run repeatedly with the specified period, in thread context. The period restarts when the callback fires, not when it returns, so a callback that runs longer than the period leaves the next firing already due. public static ulong ScheduleRecurring(Action callback, TimeSpan period) Parameters callback Action Method to invoke each period. period TimeSpan Period between firings; must be positive. Resolution is bounded by the scheduler tick. Returns ulong The alarm ID to pass to Cancel(ulong), or 0 when the alarm could not be scheduled because the scheduler is not running or the period is not positive.

articles/dev/accessing-internals.html.title: Accessing internals | Cosmos Gen 3
articles/dev/accessing-internals.html.summary: Accessing internals Everything outside the supported surface described in Public API Tracking is internal by design: visibility is not the extension mechanism, seams are. When no seam covers a need, [UnsafeAccessor] and [UnsafeAccessorType] reach internal state directly, without an InternalsVisibleTo grant. That hatch is deliberately available and deliberately unsupported: internals change in any release without notice, and code using them is expected to break. The mechanism [UnsafeAccessor] (System.Runtime.CompilerServices) declares an extern method that the runtime binds to an otherwise inaccessible member; [UnsafeAccessorType] extends it to types that are themselves inaccessible, addressed by assembly-qualified name. Both are resolved statically by ILC, so they are AOT-safe, unlike reflection, which the kernel cannot use. Accessing an internal static member of an internal type: using System.Runtime.CompilerServices; internal static class CoreAccessors { // Binds to Cosmos.Kernel.Core.Memory.Heap.Heap.Collect(). The first // parameter carries the target type by name and is passed as null for // static members. [UnsafeAccessor(UnsafeAccessorKind.StaticMethod, Name = "Collect")] internal static extern int HeapCollect( [UnsafeAccessorType("Cosmos.Kernel.Core.Memory.Heap.Heap, Cosmos.Kernel.Core")] object? heap); } int freed = CoreAccessors.HeapCollect(null); Accessing a private instance field of an accessible type: [UnsafeAccessor(UnsafeAccessorKind.Field, Name = "_name")] private static extern ref string GetName(Partition partition); UnsafeAccessorKind covers methods, static methods, constructors, and fields; property accessors are addressed as methods named get_X/set_X. Limits Byref returns of inaccessible types throw. An accessor cannot ref-return a field whose own type is inaccessible to the declaring assembly; the runtime rejects it by spec. This is why ThreadPlug does not plug Thread.CreateThread: the upstream body reads the private StartHelper, whose type cannot be byref-returned, so the seam runs below it instead (see the comment in ThreadPlug.cs). Resolution failures surface at the call site, not as a compile error: a renamed or removed target member turns the accessor into a throwing stub. Signatures must match exactly, including custom modifiers on the rare members that carry them. When to use it In order of preference: The supported surface (Cosmos.Kernel.System plus the contract interfaces). If it is missing something a kernel legitimately needs, open an issue: extending the ring is the intended fix. An [Experimental] seam where one exists (the scheduler seam, Scheduler - Writing a Scheduler). A plug, when the goal is replacing behavior rather than reaching state. [UnsafeAccessor]/[UnsafeAccessorType], accepting that any release may break it.

articles/dev/build/asm-build.html.title: | Cosmos Gen 3
articles/dev/build/asm-build.html.summary: Cosmos.Build.Asm compiles handwritten assembly sources into object files that are linked with the NativeAOT output. Both x64 and ARM64 targets use the clang integrated assembler on GAS-syntax .s files. Flow chart flowchart TD A[GetAsmTool] --> B[FindAsmSourceFiles] B --> C[BuildAsm] C --> D[.obj files under cosmos/asm] Parameters Name Description Default AsmToolPath Full path to the clang executable. Auto-detected by GetAsmTool if not set. Resolved via ResolveCosmosToolTask (system PATH + Cosmos tools bundle) AsmSearchPath One or more directories to scan (non-recursive) for *.s. none AsmFiles Explicit list of *.s files to compile (added to scan results). none AsmOutputPath Directory for compiled object files. $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/asm/ Notes: When RuntimeIdentifier is set (e.g., linux-x64), FindAsmSourceFiles will prefer an architecture subfolder if present (e.g., <searchDir>/x64/). The target triple is selected by AsmBuildTask from TargetArchitecture: x86_64-elf for x64 and aarch64-none-elf for ARM64. Tasks Task Description Depends On GetAsmTool Resolves AsmToolPath to the clang binary via ResolveCosmosToolTask. none FindAsmSourceFiles Cleans inputs, applies arch overrides, and discovers *.s under AsmSearchPath. Build BuildAsm Invokes AsmBuildTask for each file with --target=<triple> -c, writing to AsmOutputPath. FindAsmSourceFiles; GetAsmTool CleanAsm Removes $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/asm/. Clean Detailed Workflow GetAsmTool resolves AsmToolPath to a clang binary (override / system / Cosmos tools bundle). FindAsmSourceFiles: Removes any nonexistent entries from AsmSearchPath and AsmFiles (emits warnings). If RuntimeIdentifier is set, replaces any AsmSearchPath that contains a matching arch subfolder with that subfolder (e.g., x64). Builds a non-recursive search pattern %(AsmSearchPath.FullPath)/*.s and adds results to AsmFiles (deduplicated). BuildAsm calls the AsmBuildTask for each file: Computes a SHA1 of the source and emits <name>-<sha1>.obj into AsmOutputPath. Executes clang --target=<x86_64-elf|aarch64-none-elf> -c -o <output.obj> <input.s>. CleanAsm deletes the cosmos/asm intermediate folder during Clean. Outputs Object files in $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/asm/ named as <sourceName>-<sha1>.obj where <sha1> is the content hash of the source. This guarantees deterministic, cache-friendly names across builds. Related components Cosmos.Build.Asm

articles/dev/build/gcc-build.html.title: | Cosmos Gen 3
articles/dev/build/gcc-build.html.summary: Cosmos.Build.GCC compiles C sources into object files that are linked with the NativeAOT output. Flow chart flowchart TD A[GetGCC] --> B[FindCSourceFilesForGCC] B --> C[BuildGCC] C --> D[.o/.obj files under cosmos/cobj] Parameters Name Description Default GCCPath Full path or name of the gcc executable. Set by GetGCC per-OS, overridable in your project. Unix: gcc; Windows: x86_64-elf-gcc GCCProject One or more directories to scan (non-recursive) for *.c. Supports arch subfolder override. none GCCOutputPath Directory for compiled object files. $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/cobj/ GCCCompilerFlags Additional compiler flags passed to GCC. -O2 -fno-stack-protector -nostdinc -fno-builtin plus arch flags Notes: When RuntimeIdentifier is set (e.g., linux-x64), FindCSourceFilesForGCC prefers an architecture subfolder if present (e.g., <dir>/x64/). On Windows the default tool is a cross-compiler (x86_64-elf-gcc); on Unix it is gcc. You can override GCCPath. Tasks Task Description Depends On GetGCC Resolves GCCPath per OS (Unix: gcc, Windows: x86_64-elf-gcc). none FindCSourceFilesForGCC Cleans @(GCCProject) inputs and applies arch overrides. Build BuildGCC Invokes GCCBuildTask to compile each *.c in every @(GCCProject) directory. FindCSourceFilesForGCC; GetGCC CleanGCC Removes $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/cobj/. Clean Detailed workflow GetGCC sets GCCPath according to the host OS. You can override GCCPath in your project file if needed. FindCSourceFilesForGCC: Removes any nonexistent paths from @(GCCProject) (emits warnings). If RuntimeIdentifier is set and a matching arch subfolder exists (e.g., x64), the folder is replaced with that subfolder. Logs the final list of C project directories. BuildGCC: Ensures GCCOutputPath ($(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/cobj/) exists and cleans stale objects. For each @(GCCProject) directory, calls GCCBuildTask which compiles every *.c file in that directory (non-recursive). Each file is compiled individually to an object named <name>-<sha1>.(obj|o) where the hash is derived from file contents; extension is .obj on Windows, .o elsewhere. CleanGCC removes the cosmos/cobj directory during Clean. Outputs Object files in $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/cobj/ named as <sourceName>-<sha1>.(obj|o). Related components Cosmos.Build.GCC

articles/dev/build/ilc-build.html.title: | Cosmos Gen 3
articles/dev/build/ilc-build.html.summary: Overview Cosmos.ilc.Build integrates the native AOT ILCompiler into the MSBuild pipeline. It consumes patched assemblies emitted by Cosmos.Build.Patcher and transforms them into native object files later linked with platform libraries for CosmosOS. Flow chart flowchart TD A[ResolveIlcPath] --> B[WriteIlcRsp] B --> C[CompileWithIlc] C --> D[Native binary] Parameters Name Description Default IlcToolsPath Path to the ilc executable resolved from the Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler runtime pack. auto-resolved IlcIntermediateOutputPath Directory where .ilc.rsp and .o files are written. $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/native/ IlcSystemModule System module used as ILCompiler entry point. System.Private.CoreLib UnmanagedEntryPointsAssembly Assemblies whose methods are exported via --generateunmanagedentrypoints. Cosmos.Kernel.Runtime Tasks Task Description Depends On ResolveIlcPath Downloads and locates ILCompiler, setting IlcToolsPath. Build WriteIlcRsp Produces the ILCompiler response file listing inputs, references, and options. ResolveIlcPath CompileWithIlc Runs ilc using the response file to emit a native object file. WriteIlcRsp Detailed workflow ResolveIlcPath uses GetPackageDirectory to find the runtime.<RID>.Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler package and sets IlcToolsPath. WriteIlcRsp creates $(IlcIntermediateOutputPath)$(AssemblyName).ilc.rsp, gathering patched assemblies from $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos, references from cosmos/ref, and ILCompiler options such as --runtimeknob and --feature flags. CompileWithIlc executes ilc with the generated response file, producing $(AssemblyName).o in $(IlcIntermediateOutputPath). The native binary is ready for further packaging, such as bootloader integration. Outputs Response file: $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/native/$(AssemblyName).ilc.rsp listing inputs, references, and ILCompiler options. Native object: $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/native/$(AssemblyName).o produced by CompileWithIlc for linking. Notes: Reference assemblies resolved by ILC are located under $(IntermediateOutputPath)/cosmos/ref/ and come from the Patcher step. Related components Cosmos.Build.Ilc Cosmos.Build.Patcher Cosmos.Patcher
